report_status: FINAL source-verified score comparison; bounded historical-search/audit limitations
verdict: Go is the PRIMARY winner in the requested comparison using the recorded FINAL scores, including scores from runs marked INVALID. TypeScript (Bun) and Go have the two highest middle scores across four runs, 69 and 68.5 passed tests out of 106. Their gap is within three tests, so the requested timing method decides: Go takes 15.804 seconds versus TypeScript's 18.052. Sensitivities: Go also wins when all five languages within three tests of the leader are compared, when only Go's two MacBook runs are used, or when its Studio runs are replaced by the two make-ups (REPAIRED). Reading “still within the tie zone” literally gives “no clear winner,” because the score gap never changes. Excluding intervals with no build/test work gives TypeScript for the main comparison and the two-MacBook Go comparison, Rust for the all-language comparison, and Go for REPAIRED. Taking the middle of each run's timing medians instead also gives Rust for the all-language comparison; the other timing-based comparisons still give Go. PRIMARY is the registered reading (ruled by main under RULES 2); the others are sensitivities. Invalid runs, incomplete audits and unfinished searches for earlier perfect scores limit this verdict; an earlier officially verified perfect score from an eligible run could supersede it.

additional_measurement_disclosures: The configured Mac build/test caps are soft two-core limits, with five languages running concurrently. Studio efficiency cores are a hardware caveat; actual core placement and CPU bursts are not characterized in this report. The nondeciding Linux hosts have 2 vCPU and 7 GB RAM. The timing comparison is not normalized for these host differences.

Model-wait includes stalls but does not separately identify quota/rate-limit stall time. No stall-adjusted comparison is supplied here. Absence of a separate stall count should not be read as evidence that no stalls occurred.

Logged whole-second FINAL version warm-ups range from 0 to 5 seconds across the original Mac cells; both Go make-ups log 1 second, and all four Linux FINALs log 0 seconds. Every original Mac and make-up FINAL is below the 103-case lower edge of the mandatory double-scoring band, so each uses its first raw scoring. Agreement between first and combined results is not an independent repeatability check. Flakiness and clean-copy regrade differences are not characterized in this report.
